titlePl: Ósmoklasista: Człowiek — 36 haseł do gier LingoSpark
titleEn: Grade 8 English: People — 36 terms for LingoSpark games
blurbPl: Dział Człowiek na egzamin ósmoklasisty: wygląd, cechy charakteru, ubrania, emocje. Wklejasz do darmowych gier na LingoSpark.
blurbEn: Grade-8 People module: appearance, character, clothes, feelings. Paste into free LingoSpark vocab games.

items.definitionEn: having light-coloured hair
items.example: The fair-haired boy in the first row is my cousin.

items.definitionEn: hair that forms curls, not straight
items.example: She has curly hair and usually ties it in a ponytail.

items.definitionEn: small brown spots on the skin, often on the face
items.example: In summer her freckles are more visible.

items.definitionEn: hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks
items.example: My uncle grew a beard during the holidays.

items.definitionEn: thin in an attractive, healthy way
items.example: She is slim because she cycles to school every day.

items.definitionEn: heavier than is healthy or expected
items.example: The doctor said he is slightly overweight.

items.definitionEn: neither young nor old, often about 40–60
items.example: A middle-aged woman asked us for directions.

items.definitionEn: a person aged about 13 to 19
items.example: As a teenager he spent hours playing football.

items.definitionEn: two children born to the same mother at the same time
items.example: The twins wear the same jacket but different hats.

items.definitionEn: friendly and enjoying other people's company
items.example: An outgoing student quickly makes friends in a new class.

items.definitionEn: nervous about talking to people you do not know well
items.example: He is too shy to speak in front of the whole class.

items.definitionEn: always telling the truth and not cheating
items.example: Be honest if you did not do the homework.

items.definitionEn: someone you can trust to do what they promise
items.example: A reliable friend will not forget your birthday.

items.definitionEn: not willing to change your mind
items.example: She is stubborn and still wants the same phone.

items.definitionEn: happy to give time or money to others
items.example: It was generous of him to share his lunch.

items.definitionEn: unhappy because someone has something you want
items.example: Do not be jealous of her new bike — you can borrow it.

items.definitionEn: feeling silly or uncomfortable in front of others
items.example: I felt embarrassed when I said the wrong name.

items.definitionEn: pleased with what you or someone else has done
items.example: Her parents are proud of her exam results.

items.definitionEn: to have a friendly relationship with someone
items.example: I get on with my classmates, even during group work.

items.definitionEn: to have a similar appearance to someone
items.example: You look like your mother in that photo.

items.definitionEn: to be similar to an older relative in looks or character
items.example: They take after their grandfather — both are very calm.

items.definitionEn: popular at the moment in clothes or style
items.example: That jacket is fashionable this winter.

items.definitionEn: comfortable clothes for everyday life, not formal
items.example: We can wear casual clothes on Friday.

items.definitionEn: a loose jacket and trousers for sport
items.example: Put on a tracksuit before PE.

items.definitionEn: a sweatshirt with a hood
items.example: He never goes out without his grey hoodie.

items.definitionEn: comfortable shoes for sport or everyday wear
items.example: These trainers are better for running than boots.

items.definitionEn: objects such as rings, necklaces or earrings
items.example: School rules say you cannot wear jewellery in PE.

items.definitionEn: substances put on the face to change how it looks
items.example: She does not wear make-up to school.

items.definitionEn: attractive in appearance
items.example: People say the actor is very good-looking.

items.definitionEn: becoming angry easily
items.example: He is bad-tempered when he is hungry.

items.definitionEn: calm and not easily upset
items.example: Our easy-going coach never shouts during training.

items.definitionEn: sure of your own abilities
items.example: A self-confident speaker looks at the audience.

items.definitionEn: easily hurt by what other people say
items.example: Be careful — she is sensitive about her accent.

items.definitionEn: happy and showing it
items.example: A cheerful greeting makes the morning better.

items.definitionEn: to put your clothes on
items.example: Hurry up and get dressed or we will miss the bus.

items.definitionEn: to change from a child into an adult
items.example: I want to grow up in a quiet town, not a huge city.
